rationale: A wins because it does the ruthless thing B won't: it collapses the launch into three defensible reporter shapes and refuses the rest. A's "Airbnb wants the corporate travel budget, and it's routing the expenses through Concur and Ramp" turns the integration into a clean managed-travel conflict without pretending adoption exists. B has good raw material, but "Airbnb builds a travel-manager console to get short-term rentals written into company policy" and "Airbnb plugs into Concur and Ramp, putting the stay inside the expense report" are the same dashboard/billing plumbing in two costumes, and "with a tool it gives away" overreads a fact that only says free for travelers.
gaps_in_A: "Airbnb says business travel is its fastest-growing segment, up 71% - off a small base it won't size" overstates the fact block; the update withholds the base from us, but does not prove Airbnb refused to size it.

"Travel managers finally get one dashboard for Airbnb" is refused as a duplicate too quickly; with a named travel manager and policy before/after, that can be a buyer-workflow story, not just a softer version of the Concur/Ramp conflict.

"hotels, TMCs, and incumbent corporate-booking tools should treat this as a real channel threat" is the right question, but it still needs adoption or functionality proof before it becomes more than launch-day chessboarding.
gaps_in_B: "Airbnb builds a travel-manager console...", "Airbnb goes after managed corporate lodging spend...", and "Airbnb plugs into Concur and Ramp..." slice one product fact into three angles; that is padding with better shoes.

"a travel manager who has been fielding rogue Airbnb bookings on personal cards" is invented color. The update gives dashboard, billing, and integrations; it does not give rogue bookings or personal-card behavior.
"with a tool it gives away" misstates the economics. The fact is only "free for travelers"; employers, hosts, or partners may still carry cost, and B knows this because its proof list asks who pays.
"legacy expense system and a newer one" imports outside characterization of Concur and Ramp. Maybe true, but not from the supplied update, and this exercise is not a vibes memo.
